Method 2: Excel Web Queries - Built-in but Limited

Excel's native 'Get Data from Web' feature can extract basic tables but struggles with modern websites and complex layouts.

  • ❌ Fails on JavaScript-rendered content and dynamic tables
  • ❌ Cannot handle div-based table layouts
  • ❌ Requires technical setup and maintenance
  • ❌ Often breaks when website structures change

Method 3: Manual Copy-Paste - Free but Frustrating

The most common approach but leads to formatting disasters, data loss, and hours of cleanup work.

  • ❌ Tables collapse into single columns
  • ❌ Lost data and broken formatting
  • ❌ Manual cleanup required for every conversion
  • ❌ Not suitable for professional use

Method 4: Programming Solutions - Powerful but Complex

Custom scripts using Python (BeautifulSoup, Pandas) or JavaScript offer maximum flexibility but require coding skills and ongoing maintenance.

  • ❌ Requires programming knowledge
  • ❌ Setup and maintenance overhead
  • ❌ Overkill for simple conversions
  • ❌ Not practical for non-technical users
